dossier.purpose: Canonical's root-filesystem image of Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS ('Resolute Raccoon') for the Windows Subsystem for Linux: file ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.wsl (399M, modified 2026-08-27 14:17, 'WSL image for 64-bit PC (AMD64) computers'), listed at https://releases.ubuntu.com/26.04.1/ and described there as 'the root filesystem to be installed and launched by the Windows Subsystem for Linux'. Context pages: the Ubuntu on WSL docs landing page (the listed https://documentation.ubuntu.com/wsl/latest/ answers 301 to https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/, which is the page actually read) and the Ubuntu release-cycle table (https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle). This is not a source repository: the working directory held only .round-meta.json, so there is no README, code, tag, commit or license file, and nothing could be checked against code; the README, install, platform and claim fields are filled from the three listed pages only. Pages were read with WebFetch, which summarizes, so quotes are as returned and may not be byte-exact; key values were cross-checked across 2 to 4 separate fetches. Not opened because they are outside the three listed pages: SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.gpg, the *.manifest files, and every sub-page linked from the docs landing page (install how-to, CUDA how-to, data collection, firewall, distributions). This entry's 'repository' URL (https://ubuntu.com/download/server) is not in the page list and was not opened. The pages say nothing about any particular host; the one fact that bears on which image would be installed is that the /26.04.1/ directory lists two WSL images: ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.wsl (399M, 2026-08-27 14:17) and ubuntu-26.04-wsl-amd64.wsl (396M, 2026-04-20 18:09).

claims.claim: Page title and heading: 'Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Resolute Raccoon)'. The WSL section states: 'The WSL image is the root filesystem to be installed and launched by the Windows Subsystem for Linux.'

The link '64-bit PC (AMD64) WSL image' has href 'ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.wsl' (relative; full URL https://releases.ubuntu.com/26.04.1/ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.wsl). Its table row: modified 2026-08-27 14:17, 399M, 'WSL image for 64-bit PC (AMD64) computers (standard download)'. Companion ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.manifest: 16K, same timestamp, '(contents of live filesystem)'.

The same table also lists ubuntu-26.04-wsl-amd64.wsl (2026-04-20 18:09, 396M, '(standard download)') and ubuntu-26.04-wsl-amd64.manifest (16K), so two WSL images are present in the /26.04.1/ directory (13 files per version: 26.04 and 26.04.1, plus SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.gpg and a netboot/ directory). No .torrent or .zsync is listed for either .wsl file (only for the ISOs).

Checksum files: SHA256SUMS (size column 588, 2026-08-27 22:43) and SHA256SUMS.gpg (833, 2026-08-27 22:43) are listed with empty description cells. The page has no sentence about verifying downloads, checksums, GPG or SHA256; its only help links are BitTorrent, Image Burning Guide and zsync.

Every image listed is AMD64 (page text: 'Choose this if you have a computer based on the AMD64 or EM64T architecture ... Choose this if you are at all unsure.'). The page opens with 'Ubuntu is distributed on eight types of images described below.' but has four image-type sections (Desktop image, Server install image, Netboot tarball, WSL image). Footer: '© 2025 Canonical Ltd. Ubuntu and Canonical are registered trademarks of Canonical Ltd.'

'Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) enables developers to run a GNU/Linux environment on Windows.' and 'Ubuntu on WSL provides a fully-featured Ubuntu experience on Windows, suitable for learning Linux, developing a personal open-source project, or building for production in an enterprise environment.'

'Ubuntu Pro for WSL is a tool for managing Ubuntu on WSL. It enables automatic attachment of your Pro subscription to Ubuntu instances, and remote deployment with Landscape.' Ubuntu on WSL is described as 'an open-source project'.

Landing-page navigation (link titles only; targets not opened) includes: Install Ubuntu on WSL; Upgrade Ubuntu; Automatic setup of Ubuntu with cloud-init; Customize an Ubuntu image for WSL; Enabling GPU acceleration with CUDA; Ubuntu distributions; WSL instance configuration; Firewall requirements for Ubuntu on WSL; Comparing WSL versions for Ubuntu on WSL; Security overview for Ubuntu on WSL; Data collection and Ubuntu on WSL; GitHub actions for Ubuntu WSL; QA process.

The landing-page prose never mentions 'WSL 2'/'WSL2'/'WSL 1', systemd, NVIDIA, checksum, download, Microsoft Store, 'wsl --install', Windows 10/11, LTS or any Ubuntu release number. CUDA, cloud-init and data collection occur only inside link titles. 'latest' is the only version label; no last-updated date is shown.

26.04 LTS row: Released Apr 2026; Standard security maintenance May 2031; and, under the 'Ubuntu Pro' column group, Expanded security maintenance May 2036, Break/bug support May 2036, Legacy add-on for security maintenance and support May 2041.

'LTS are released every two years and receive 5 years of standard security maintenance' (CVE patches for packages in Main). ESM 'extends the life of LTS releases by providing 10 years of security updates for the Main repository and also adds 10 years of security coverage for the Universe repository.' The Legacy add-on 'can be purchased' at the end of the 10-year ESM period to cover an additional 5 years (15 in total).
'Ubuntu Pro subscriptions are free for personal use on up to five machines.' Ubuntu Pro is described as 'Canonical's enhanced security and support subscription for Ubuntu systems.'

Architectures listed for 26.04 LTS: 'amd64, armhf, arm64, s390x, riscv64, ppc64el-p9'. The page contains no point-release information and no 26.04.1 date (searches for point release, WSL, Windows and HWE found nothing).

code.architecture: No source tree is in scope. From the listed pages: the release directory https://releases.ubuntu.com/26.04.1/ is a flat file index holding, for each of 26.04 and 26.04.1, a desktop ISO and a live-server ISO (each with .torrent/.zsync/.list/.manifest), a netboot tarball, and a WSL image (.wsl plus .manifest), plus top-level SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.gpg and a netboot/ directory. The .wsl artifact is described only as 'the root filesystem to be installed and launched by the Windows Subsystem for Linux'; its init system, default packages and user configuration are not described on any listed page. The Ubuntu on WSL docs (https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/) use the Diataxis structure and link to a separate docs host (canonical-ubuntu-on-wsl.readthedocs-hosted.com). They also cover Ubuntu Pro for WSL, whose reference pages are titled 'Windows Agent CLI' and 'WSL Pro Service CLI' (link titles only; not opened).
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts per the listing (https://releases.ubuntu.com/26.04.1/): ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.wsl and .manifest (both 2026-08-27 14:17), SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.gpg (both 2026-08-27 22:43, i.e. later than the WSL image). Neither checksum row has a description, and the page gives no verification instructions. No provenance, attestation or SBOM is mentioned on the listed pages beyond the .manifest ('contents of live filesystem'). No release workflow can be cited: the build pipeline is not described on the listed pages (the docs landing page links 'Customize an Ubuntu image for WSL' and 'GitHub actions for Ubuntu WSL', not opened). The release-cycle page gives no 26.04.1 date; the only date evidence is the directory timestamps (26.04.1 files 2026-08-26/27, 26.04 files 2026-04-20/23).
code.tests_and_ci: None found on the listed pages (no repository in scope). The docs landing page links 'QA process' and 'Run a WSL GitHub workflow on Azure' (not opened) - https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/
code.dependencies: No manifest files in scope; direct dependency count not applicable. The package list of the image would be in ubuntu-26.04.1-wsl-amd64.manifest (16K), which was not opened, so Python, Node and Rust versions in the image are not established by the listed pages.
code.security_policy: none (no SECURITY.md or repository in scope). Related statements: the support phases and dates on https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle; the docs landing page links 'Security overview for Ubuntu on WSL' (not opened).

The docs landing page only links 'Enabling GPU acceleration with CUDA', 'Install Ubuntu on WSL' and 'Comparing WSL versions for Ubuntu on WSL' (not opened), and the image's package list (.manifest, 16K) was not opened. https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/ ; https://releases.ubuntu.com/26.04.1/

Long-term support is tiered: standard security maintenance (to May 2031) covers packages in Main. ESM (to May 2036, adding Universe), break/bug support (May 2036) and the Legacy add-on (May 2041) sit under an 'Ubuntu Pro' column group. Pro is 'free for personal use on up to five machines'; terms for other use were not read, and the pages do not say whether any given toolchain package is in Main or Universe. https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle

Docs location and versioning are unclear: https://documentation.ubuntu.com/wsl/latest/ answers 301 to https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/, whose sub-pages link to a third host (canonical-ubuntu-on-wsl.readthedocs-hosted.com). The page shows only a 'latest' label, no version or last-updated date, and names no Ubuntu release, so it is undetermined which Ubuntu release the docs describe. https://ubuntu.com/wsl/docs/latest/

Source-quality caveats: the releases page says 'eight types of images' but describes four, and carries a '© 2025' footer on a 2026 listing, which suggests reused template text. The pages were read through a summarizing fetcher: the first query omitted the 26.04 rows that later queries returned, and one query reported 31 table rows where the table text from another query has 29. Exact values should be re-read from the live pages. https://releases.ubuntu.com/26.04.1/
